# Rule catalog - `copy-check.mjs`

<!-- GENERATED by `node scripts/copy-check.mjs --rules-md` from scripts/lib/rules.mjs; edit the rule records, then regenerate. -->

What a project reads before promoting a rule: its issue type, its shipped severity, what its
precision was the last time someone counted, and the false positives it is guarded against.
Severity here is the default; the contract's `rules` object overrides it per project
(copy-quality-gates/severity-as-declared-data). A rule enters as `warn` and is promoted only when its
precision is counted on the catalog and its existing occurrences are zero.

`granularity`: `word` findings compete for their span (one span, one finding: a warning overlapping a
higher-ranked finding is dropped; rank is severity, then `priority`, then span length; an error is never
dropped). `char` and `unit` findings never compete. `status: temp_off` keeps a rule's data, guards and
tests but never fires - the retire-without-delete state.

## EN-ARTIFACT

- kind `markup`, default `error`, status `on`, priority 100, granularity `word`, reads unmasked text
- precision: uncounted
- fires on: "See the report :contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}"; "Certainly! Here's your hiring plan."; "Contact [Company Name] for details."
- stays silent on: "Here's how it works."
- guards:
  - in the rule: a numeric footnote marker such as [1] - citation markers are matched by their generator-specific shapes only; seen: rule design; control: "Footnote [1] applies to annual plans."

## EN-SPELLING

- kind `locale-convention`, default `error`, status `on`, priority 90, granularity `word`
- precision: uncounted (2026-09-14) - first real-catalog run: 9 false positives from "analyses" plus proper-name hits (total findings not recorded); guarded since, not recounted
- fires on: "Customise your colour palette"; "Built on public labour-market data"; "Optimize the catalog [contract {"variant":"UK"}]"
- stays silent on: "Customize your color palette"; "Docs at https://example.com/colour-guide and file theme_colour.css"; "Optimise the catalogue [contract {"variant":"UK"}]"
- guards:
  - in the rule: "-yses" forms are not paired - "analyses" is also the US plural of the noun "analysis"; seen: first real-catalog run, 2026-09-14 (9 false positives); control: "Recruiter time-per-hire analyses and cost reports"
  - in the rule: a capitalized word inside a run of capitalized words mid-sentence - a proper name keeps its own spelling; terms.accept is the explicit cure; seen: first real-catalog run, 2026-09-14 ("Czech Labour Office"); control: "Openings registered at the Czech Labour Office every week"
  - in the rule: program, license, practice, check, tire, curb, analog, dial in a UK contract - valid British forms for a distinct sense or in software; seen: english subject exception; control: "Install the program and check the licence [contract {"variant":"UK"}]"
  - in the rule: -ize and -yze under spelling "oxford" - Oxford spelling is British with -ize; seen: english subject exception; control: "Organize your analyses [contract {"variant":"UK","spelling":"oxford"}]"

## EN-PUFFERY

- kind `style`, default `warn`, status `on`, priority 36, granularity `word`
- precision: uncounted (2026-09-14) - first real-catalog run: "robust" in its statistics sense was a false positive (count not recorded); guarded since, not recounted
- fires on: "Seamless and robust sync for every team."; "Unlock growth [key hero.title]"
- stays silent on: "A robust estimator of the median."; "Rank by the robust cross-scheme mean instead [key jobs.fairRankTitle]"
- guards:
  - executable: `/(?<![\p{L}])robust(?=\s*(?:[=:(−-]|(?:[\w]+-[\w-]+\s+)?(?:mean|median|estimat\w*|statistic\w*|regression|standard errors?|variance|average|aggregate|to outliers|against\b)))/iu` - "robust" as a statistics or engineering term, not a claim; seen: first real-catalog run, 2026-09-14; control: "Own = own weights; Robust = mean across schemes; delta = robust - own."
  - in the rule: one puffery word outside a heading - a single word in body copy is often literal ("unlock the door"); density or a heading makes it a claim; seen: rule design; control: "Unlock the door with your badge [key help.body]"

## EN-REDUNDANCY

- kind `redundancy`, default `warn`, status `on`, priority 60, granularity `word`
- precision: 0 of 1 (2026-09-14) - eight fleet trees, read by the implementing worker (not a project owner): 1 hit, "Advance warning" as a feature label - a false positive, guarded; 0 hits since
- fires on: "Because of the fact that the import is completely finished, the end result arrives."; "Claim your free gift today."; "We report on a daily basis."
- stays silent on: "The import is done, so the report arrives within a minute."
- guards:
  - in the rule: "advance warning" and "advance notice" are not listed - "advance" separates a warning before expiry from an alert at expiry, and "30 days' advance notice" is contract language; seen: personas-web, wave-3 fleet run 2026-09-14; control: "Advance warning for non-refresh credentials: a yellow status N days before expiry."
  - executable: `/future plans?(?=[^.!?]{0,60}\b(?:pricing|price|tiers?|seats?|billing|subscriptions?|per month|monthly|annual|upgrade|downgrade)\b)|(?<=\b(?:pricing|price|tiers?|seats?|billing|subscriptions?|upgrade|downgrade)\b[^.!?]{0,60})future plans?/iu` - "plans" as pricing tiers: a future plan is a tier not yet offered, not a pleonasm; seen: rule design (SaaS pricing copy); control: "Upgrade now; future plans will change the per month price."
  - executable: `/“[^”]{1,300}”|"[^"\n]{1,300}"/u` - quoted speech is evidence, not voice (english subject exception); seen: english subject; control: "A customer wrote: “the end result speaks for itself.”"
